premises: Dynamic behavior in FeNiCrMn is governed by competition between dislocation slip and mechanical twinning.
This competition is controlled by temperature- and strain-rate-dependent variations in stacking fault energy.
Reduced effective stacking fault energy promotes mechanical twinning, enhancing strain hardening and ductility.
At extreme conditions (very low temperatures or high strain rates), dislocation slip dominates as twin formation is suppressed.
The mechanistic role of twin formation in enhancing mechanical performance is supported by previous work on similar alloys.
